door.ldap: an LDAP simple bind on 389 or 636 (RFC 4513)
door.wstrust: a WS-Security UsernameToken sent to the security token service
fresh.heading: Your new app password
fresh.copyNow: Copy it now. It is shown on this page once and cannot be shown again — this service keeps only a hash of it.
fresh.note: Put it in the client in place of your password, with your usual username. It works only at the doors above and never at the sign-in screen. The dashes are optional.
th.name: Name
doors.heading: Where a password alone is asked for
doors.either: your password, or an app password
doors.leadNoFactor: You hold no second factor, so your own password is accepted at these doors. An app password is still worth having: it is random, it works only where you say, and revoking one does not change your password.
doors.leadDevelopment: This service is in development mode and checks no password at these doors. In product mode, because you use a second factor, your own password would be refused there and an app password is what you would use.
doors.leadRefused: Because you use a second factor, your own password is refused at the doors marked below — they cannot ask for the second factor. Make an app password for each client that uses one of them.
list.heading: Your app passwords
list.note: Revoking one stops the client that holds it at its next sign-in. The id is the first four characters of the password; it is not secret.
create.heading: Make an app password
create.off: App passwords are turned off here, so a new one cannot be made. The ones you have go on working.
create.note: It is shown once, on the page that answers this form. Choose only the doors the client needs.
